title: Comparison homomorphism from the positive integral form to Borel distributions
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme], semisimple (having no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup) and simply connected (every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism). Solvable means its iterated commutator subgroup schemes become trivial, and finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting over every commutative $F$-algebra. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, a Borel $B$, its unipotent radical $U$, and positive roots $\Phi^+$ with simple base $\Delta$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For each $\alpha\in\Delta$ prescribe any group-scheme isomorphism $x_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to U_\alpha$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Put $\epsilon:F[U]\to F$ for evaluation at $1$, $\mathfrak m=\ker\epsilon$, and
$$H=\bigcup_{d\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_F(F[U]/\mathfrak m^{d+1},F),\qquad (ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta_U f),$$
where $\Delta_U$ is the coordinate coproduct of multiplication. There exist a finite-dimensional split semisimple rational Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Chevalley basis $h_i,e_\gamma$ in the precise conventions of [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw], an identification of its based root system with $(\Phi,\Delta)$, and choices of group-scheme isomorphisms $x_\beta:\mathbf G_a\to U_\beta$ for every $\beta\in\Phi^+$ extending the prescribed simple ones, with the following property. Define $U_{\mathbf Q}=T_{\mathbf Q}(\mathfrak g)/(xy-yx-[x,y])$, $e_\beta^{(m)}=e_\beta^m/m!$, and let $K_{\mathbf Z}^+\subseteq U_{\mathbf Q}$ be the unital $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by all $e_\beta^{(m)}$ with $\beta\in\Phi^+$ and $m\geq0$. There is a unital $F$-algebra homomorphism
$$\Psi:F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}K_{\mathbf Z}^+\longrightarrow H$$
satisfying
$$\Psi(1\otimes e_\beta^{(m)})(f)=[t^m]x_\beta^*f\qquad(\beta\in\Phi^+,\ m\geq0,\ f\in F[U]).$$
The assertion allows any prime, including bad primes for the root system, and the empty root system. It does not identify $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathfrak g_{\mathbf Z}$ with $\operatorname{Lie}(S)$.

source.place: Section 1, printed pp.150--151: integral form generated by simple divided powers and its hyperalgebra realization. Read online at https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf; the local PDF is WANTED. Agent-stated bridge from the geometric group to the integral hyperalgebra model. Local supporting source: literature/milne-algebraic-groups_iAG2017.pdf, Section 23h, equation (153), pp.509--511, and the integral-group-model paragraph on p.511. Full coordinate-duality proof WANTED: Kostant, Groups over Z (1966), or Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups (1967).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-root-model] to $S,T,B$ and the prescribed simple root maps. Retain its $\mathcal G,\mathcal U,y_\gamma,\iota$ and rational Chevalley Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Set $x_\beta=\iota\circ(y_\beta)_F$ for positive roots. These are the required root isomorphisms and extend all prescribed simple maps. Write $A=\mathbf Z[\mathcal U]$, $I=\ker(A\to\mathbf Z)$ and $L=\bigcup_d\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A/I^{d+1},\mathbf Z)$. The model's ordered root chart identifies $(A,I)$ with $(\mathbf Z[t_1,\ldots,t_N],(t_1,\ldots,t_N))$. Thus $A/I^{d+1}$ has the finite basis $t^a$ with $|a|\le d$, and $L$ has basis the coefficient functionals $\delta_a=[t^a]$, with every element a finite sum.

source.place: Section 10l, p.208, and Section 23h, pp.509--511; agent coordinate-duality construction of the integral comparison

proof.text: Give $L$ convolution using the integral coproduct of $\mathcal U$. The counit splitting $A=\mathbf Z\oplus I$ shows $\Delta(I)\subseteq I\otimes A+A\otimes I$. In an $(a+b+1)$-fold product of such terms, either at least $a+1$ factors belong to the first copy of $I$ or at least $b+1$ to the second. Consequently the convolution of functionals of orders at most $a,b$ kills $I^{a+b+1}$. It is integer-valued, so lies in $L$. Coassociativity and the counit identities give associativity and unit. For a positive root put $d_{\beta,m}(f)=[t^m]y_\beta^*f$. Because $y_\beta^*I\subseteq(t)$, this is an element of $L$ of order at most $m$.

source.place: Section 10l, p.208, and Section 23h, pp.509--511; agent coordinate-duality construction of the integral comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-characteristic-zero-distribution-enveloping] to $\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q}$ to obtain $\Theta:U_{\mathbf Q}(\mathfrak g)\to\operatorname{Dist}(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q})$. In $\operatorname{Dist}(\mathbf G_{a,\mathbf Q})$, let $q_m=[t^m]$. The coproduct $t\mapsto t\otimes1+1\otimes t$ gives $q_aq_b=\binom{a+b}{a}q_{a+b}$, hence $q_1^m=m!q_m$, including $m=0$. The model identifies $d(y_\beta)_{\mathbf Q}(1)$ with $e_\beta$. The naturality clause, applied to $y_\beta$, therefore gives $\Theta(e_\beta^m/m!)=(y_\beta)_{\mathbf Q,*}q_m$. This division takes place solely over $\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Section 10l, p.208, and Section 23h, pp.509--511; agent coordinate-duality construction of the integral comparison

proof.text: There is an injective unital ring homomorphism $j:L\to\operatorname{Dist}(\mathcal G_{\mathbf Q})$: extend a functional rationally on $A\otimes\mathbf Q$ and precompose with restriction from $\mathbf Q[\mathcal G]$. Rational extension is injective by the coefficient basis of Step 1. Restriction is surjective because the model makes $\mathcal U\hookrightarrow\mathcal G$ a closed immersion, so its dual is injective. Both operations respect the coproduct and counit, hence convolution and unit. Step 3 says $\Theta(e_\beta^{(m)})=j(d_{\beta,m})$. The image $j(L)$ is a unital integer subalgebra by Step 2 and contains all these generator images. Since $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$ is the integer algebra generated by them, $\Theta(K_{\mathbf Z}^+)\subseteq j(L)$. For $k\in K_{\mathbf Z}^+$ define $\theta(k)$ to be the unique preimage of $\Theta(k)$ in $L$. Injectivity of $j$ proves that $\theta$ preserves sums, products and unit and sends $e_\beta^{(m)}$ to $d_{\beta,m}$. In particular all integral relations are respected, without any claimed presentation of $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$.

source.place: Section 10l, p.208, and Section 23h, pp.509--511; agent coordinate-duality construction of the integral comparison

proof.text: The coefficient basis supplies an $F$-linear bijection $b:F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\to\operatorname{Dist}(\mathcal U_F)$: send $c\otimes\delta_a$ to $c[t^a]$ on $F[t_1,\ldots,t_N]$. Both sides consist exactly of finite sums of these coefficient functionals. To check multiplicativity, evaluate on an integral monomial $f$: write $\Delta(f)=\sum_{a,b}n_{a,b}t^a\otimes t^b$, with $n_{a,b}\in\mathbf Z$ and only finitely many terms. Convolution of $\delta_a,\delta_b$ evaluates to $n_{a,b}$ before scalar extension and to its image in $F$ afterwards. This proves multiplicativity on basis elements, hence on every pair by bilinearity; the same evaluation proves preservation of the counit unit. Thus $b$ is a unital algebra isomorphism. It sends $1\otimes d_{\beta,m}$ to $[t^m](y_\beta)_F^*$, since coefficient extraction on an integral polynomial commutes with scalar extension.

source.place: Section 10l, p.208, and Section 23h, pp.509--511; agent coordinate-duality construction of the integral comparison

proof.text: Transport distributions along the model isomorphism $\iota|_{\mathcal U_F}:\mathcal U_F\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ by precomposition on functions. Its inverse makes this an algebra isomorphism, since $\iota$ respects multiplication and identity. Compose it with $b\circ(F\otimes\theta)$ to define $\Psi$. For $f\in F[U]$ the value of $\Psi(1\otimes e_\beta^{(m)})$ is $[t^m](y_\beta)_F^*\iota^*f=[t^m]x_\beta^*f$, as required. The rational Lie algebra and based-root identification were supplied in Step 1. For the empty root system the model is trivial, $A=L=\mathbf Z$, $\mathfrak g=0$ and $K_{\mathbf Z}^+=\mathbf Z$, so the same construction is the identity $F\to F$. No step divides by a scalar in $F$ or uses a positive-characteristic identification of Lie algebras.
